summary.intent: Build and test a staging desktop release (DMG) for CipherBox locally before pushing to CI, then create a fix PR for the staging environment configuration.
summary.outcome: Successfully built and tested a staging DMG locally with `VITE_API_URL=https://api-staging.cipherbox.cc` passed at compile time. PR #464 was created on branch `fix/desktop-release-staging-env` and the GitHub Actions workflow file was renamed to `desktop-staging-release.yml`.

repo: The Tauri desktop app (CipherBox v0.39.0) builds to `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/target/release/bundle/dmg/` (repo root `target/`, not under `apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/`).

The build reports exit code 1 due to missing `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`, but the DMG artifact is fully built before that error — the signing key is only needed for the auto-updater signature, not the binary itself.
PR #462 was already merged before #464 was created; its `NETWORK_MAP` change in `auth.ts` is harmless since `VITE_ENVIRONMENT=staging` never hits the `production` branch.
The GitHub Actions workflow for desktop staging releases was renamed to `desktop-staging-release.yml` as part of this PR.

Vite env vars in `.env` are read by the Vite/frontend build only — they are NOT forwarded to `cargo build`, so `option_env!("VITE_API_URL")` in Rust resolves to `None` locally unless the var is exported in the shell before running `pnpm tauri build`.

code.finding: Rust backend uses `option_env!("VITE_API_URL")` at compile time to set the API base URL, falling back to `http://localhost:3000`. This only works when `VITE_API_URL` is set as a process-level env var before `cargo build` runs — Vite's `.env` file does not populate it for Cargo.

Workflow was renamed to `desktop-staging-release.yml` to better reflect its purpose. CI sets `VITE_API_URL` as a process-level env var, which is why the Rust `option_env!` macro works in CI but not in local builds using only `.env`.

workflow: To build the Tauri desktop app locally targeting staging, you must export `VITE_API_URL` in the shell: `VITE_API_URL=https://api-staging.cipherbox.cc pnpm --filter desktop build`.
A Tauri build exit code 1 caused by a missing signing key does not mean the DMG was not produced — always check for the artifact before concluding the build failed.
pnpm workspaces: use `pnpm --filter desktop build` to scope the build to the desktop app only.

friction: Initial build without `VITE_API_URL` exported caused the Rust backend to fall back to `localhost:3000`, requiring a full Rust recompile (~23s) to fix after discovering the issue at runtime.
DMG output path was not where expected (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/`) — it builds to the monorepo root `target/` directory, causing confusion when trying to locate the artifact.
The `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` error causes the build command to exit with code 1 even though all artifacts are successfully produced, making it ambiguous whether the build succeeded.
open_items: Consider changing the Rust fallback API URL from `http://localhost:3000` to the staging URL so local builds without an exported env var default to staging rather than localhost.
The `unused import: Manager` warning in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:13` should be cleaned up.
The large chunk size warning (1,628 kB JS bundle) in the Vite build should be addressed with code splitting or `manualChunks` configuration.
